chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Is wudu (ablution) to be performed because of food, or drinking milk—the milk of cattle, camels, and sheep—and their urine and their meat? He said: “Wudu (ablution) is not performed because of it.”

key_terms.أَبْوَالِهَا: their urine; referring to the urine of the mentioned animals
key_terms.أَلْبَانِ: milks; the milk of specified animals
key_terms.اللَّبَنِ: milk; here referring to animal milk
key_terms.شُرْبِ: drinking; the act of consuming a beverage
key_terms.لُحُومِهَا: their meat; the flesh of the mentioned animals
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: to perform wudu (ablution); here, to renew ritual ablution

ai.seo_question: Does eating food or drinking animal milk require wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about what does not invalidate wudu (ablution). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that eating food, drinking the milk of cattle, camels, and sheep, and consuming their meat or contact with their urine does not necessitate wudu (ablution).
